summary: All 53 requirements are implemented and traced (258 trace entries). The controller is a 5-mode machine with 34 transitions. Each is triggered by one of eight per-cycle events the unit monitor derives from the transmission; every mode has an event-only transition. Guards are flat conjunctions of 4 boolean sensor facts and 3 controller booleans. The controller decides the mode, the pump command, the valve and PROGRAM_READY; the transmission stage sends MODE(m) and the pump orders. Failure detection, unit bookkeeping, estimation and the failure/repair protocol are in UnitMonitor. 12 points the requirements leave open are listed below.

issues.title: Boiler, steam and pump constants have no values in the requirements
issues.raw: SB-DM1..DM3 name C, M1, M2, N1, N2, W, U1, U2, P without values. Chosen: C=1000, M1=150, M2=850, N1=400, N2=600 (litre); W=25 (l/s); U1=U2=4 (l/s/s); P=10 (l/s). They respect M1<N1<N2<M2<=C, the DM1 danger statements (M1-5W>0, M2+4*5P>C) and N2+4*5P<M2. The constants are used by the unit monitor; the controller sees only the outcome of the comparisons.
issues.fix_directive: Replace with the plant's real constants if known.

issues.title: Pumps are expected closed until the program orders otherwise
issues.raw: SB-FR1/FR2 judge pumps against the program's orders, but nothing says what state a pump has before any order. The monitor assumes closed and not flowing; detection starts with STEAM_BOILER_WAITING (SB-Beh2). A repaired pump is expected to keep its reported state, and its controller gets two transmissions to settle, as after an order.
issues.fix_directive: If pumps may start open, take the first reported state as the baseline instead.

issues.title: One input event per cycle, classified by the unit monitor; other facts read through the sensor service
issues.raw: SB-V3 makes all of a cycle's messages simultaneous, and PUMP_STATE(n,b) carries two values. The messages (SB-DM9) go to UnitMonitor's receive methods. The monitor analyses the transmission and steps the controller with exactly one event, in order of precedence: StopConfirmed (STOP on 3 successive transmissions), TransmissionFault; in initialisation StartUpFailure (level device failed, or steam not zero, once STEAM_BOILER_WAITING has arrived); outside it LevelRisk; in rescue EstimateUnreliable (steam device or a pump controller failed); then SteamBoilerWaiting (first arrival), PhysicalUnitsReady (legitimate answer to PROGRAM_READY), Transmission. Every condition that only ever leads to emergency stop is thus an event-only transition. The remaining facts are four booleans in BoilerSensor (level device out of order, another unit out of order, level too low, level too high). Guards are flat conjunctions of these and 3 controller booleans, and the branches of a mode are mutually exclusive for each event (checked over all assignments). There are 34 transitions, all triggered by an event. A cycle that matches no branch changes nothing, exactly as an explicit do-nothing branch would. This shape is the result of iterations 1-4, where FDR4 ran out of memory and Isabelle's deadlock-freedom proof timed out on larger models.

issues.title: Failure detection, unit status, STOP count, level estimate and the failure/repair protocol live in UnitMonitor, outside the extracted state machine
issues.raw: Actions in the profile cannot be conditional, and every controller field becomes a model state variable. Per-unit bookkeeping, per-unit announcements and real-valued history would multiply branches and state space (iterations 1 to 4: FDR4 ran out of memory). SB-V5..V10 and SB-FR1..FR7 are implemented in Java but are not verified by the model checkers.
issues.fix_directive: Accept, or move selected bookkeeping into the controller if the model must cover it.

issues.title: Regulation switches all four pumps together, on the predicted worst-case level
issues.raw: SB-Beh10 leaves the pump policy open. The controller keeps one pump command (pumpsOpen) for all four pumps. In normal, degraded and rescue modes it orders the pumps open when the level is 'too low' and closed when it is 'too high'. The monitor judges these against the level predicted until the next transmission: it could fall below N1, or it could rise above N2 without being able to fall below N1. This anticipates the one-cycle start-up latency (SB-Beh25). In initialisation the same two facts compare the reading q with N1 and N2 (SB-Beh4/5/7). The transmission stage sends OPEN_PUMP(n)/CLOSE_PUMP(n) to every pump whose last order differs from the command. The limit risk (LevelRisk) is computed with the pumps closed when the controller will close them, and as they are otherwise; the monitor thus embeds the controller's regulation rule. In a simulation under maximal steam, the level oscillates between about 220 and 550 l, with no emergency stop.
issues.fix_directive: A finer policy (per-pump counts) would narrow the oscillation at the cost of more transitions.

issues.title: Initialisation: all four pumps fill; the valve closes one cycle before filling or PROGRAM_READY
issues.raw: SB-Beh5 says 'activates a pump'; all four are ordered open. Nothing happens before STEAM_BOILER_WAITING (SB-Beh2); the adjustment starts on the cycle after its arrival, while the steam and level checks already apply in the arrival cycle (StartUpFailure). When the level stops being above N2, the valve is closed first, and filling or PROGRAM_READY follow on the next cycle. After PROGRAM_READY no adjustment is made until PHYSICAL_UNITS_READY. An abort leaves the valve as it is (the environment takes over, SB-Beh22).
issues.fix_directive: Open a single pump instead if 'a pump' is meant literally.

issues.title: SB-Beh3 is a steam-device failure judgement
issues.raw: In initialisation, once STEAM_BOILER_WAITING has arrived, a steam reading other than zero marks the steam device out of order (and STEAM_FAILURE_DETECTION is announced); the cycle is delivered as StartUpFailure, and the controller goes to emergency stop.

issues.title: MODE on every cycle (SB-Beh24) vs. the program stopping in emergency stop (SB-Beh22)
issues.raw: Resolved for SB-Beh24: MODE(m) is sent by the transmission stage on every cycle, in every mode. In emergency stop the control task has ended (SB-Beh22): the program analyses nothing and sends nothing else, but goes on announcing MODE(emergency_stop). In the model this is an event-only self-loop of EMERGENCY_STOP with no action.
issues.fix_directive: If the program must fall silent in emergency stop, drop the MODE message there (the self-loop can stay).

issues.title: Which messages are 'aberrant' (SB-FR5)
issues.raw: Treated as transmission failures: a data message missing or duplicated; a pump number outside 1..4; STEAM_BOILER_WAITING outside initialisation; PHYSICAL_UNITS_READY other than in initialisation after PROGRAM_READY; a repair notice for a unit not out of order; a failure acknowledgement with no pending announcement.
issues.fix_directive: Relax any of these if the physical units may legitimately repeat a message.

issues.title: Level-device dynamics check and estimate
issues.raw: The evacuation valve's rate is not given, so SB-FR3's dynamic check is skipped during initialisation (static [0, C] check only). Elsewhere a reading must lie within [lower bound - max steam, upper bound + open pumps - min steam] since the last transmission. The rescue estimate (SB-V8) is a lower/upper bound advanced by worst-case steam and the water of sound pumps that stayed open.
issues.fix_directive: Supply the valve's outflow rate to enable the dynamic check during initialisation.

issues.title: Simultaneous level failure and steam/pump-controller failure in normal or degraded mode
issues.raw: Per SB-FR8, the steam/pump-controller conditions demand emergency stop only in rescue mode (EstimateUnreliable is delivered only there). Normal and degraded therefore go to rescue first, and rescue stops at the next cycle.
issues.fix_directive: Add steam/pump-controller emergency branches to normal/degraded if an immediate stop is wanted.

issues.title: Separate enum for the MODE(m) value
issues.raw: ModeValue (SB-DM10) mirrors OperatingMode (SB-V2) with distinct literal names, so the names of the payload enumeration do not coincide with the state names in the model.

next_step: Run the verification pipeline; fix the Java from the phase reports.
